_readme: Add livestream links here — this whole section only appears in the app while a basho is actually live (see Schedule.getLive in js/schedule.js), and shows a 'back for the next basho' message otherwise.
Each entry: { "id", "platform", "label", plus platform-specific fields below }. 'id' just needs to be unique in this file.

platform: "youtube" — set "channelId" to the channel's UC... ID (Channel URL -> right-click -> View Page Source -> search "channelId", or use a lookup tool like https://commentpicker.com/youtube-channel-id.php). Live status is checked automatically, no API key needed — the app asks YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint whether https://www.youtube.com/channel/<channelId>/live currently resolves to a live video. You do not need to flip anything manually for YouTube entries.

platform: "twitch" — set "channelName" to the Twitch username (the part after twitch.tv/). Twitch doesn't offer a public, keyless way to check live status from a browser (their live API requires an app Client-ID + access token), so this app CANNOT auto-detect Twitch live status out of the box. Toggle "assumeLive": true while you know the stream is running, and back to false when it ends — the pixel 'OFFLINE' card shows automatically whenever assumeLive is false.
platform: "generic" — for any other platform's embeddable player. Set "embedUrl" to the full iframe embed URL. Same limitation as Twitch: no auto-detection, so control it with "assumeLive".

Delete this _readme block or leave it — it's ignored at runtime, only "streams" is read. The two example entries below are marked "disabled": true so they're skipped at runtime and don't try to embed a fake channel — copy one, fill in your own IDs, and delete (or flip) "disabled".
